title: Compatible bounded-above flat replacements of good truncations

from.place: The existence of a K-flat resolution: compatible bounded-above replacements and their telescope comparison

lean.statement: theorem exists_flat_truncation_tower {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}} (G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) ℤ) : ∃ (E : ℕ → CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) ℤ) (t : ∀ n : ℕ, E n ⟶ E (n + 1)) (q : ∀ n : ℕ, E n ⟶ G.truncLE (n : ℤ)), (∀ n : ℕ, ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero ((E n).X i)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ), SheafOfModules.IsFlat ((E n).X i)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, QuasiIso (q n)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ), Epi ((q n).f i)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, t n ≫ q (n + 1) ≫ G.ιTruncLE ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = q n ≫ G.ιTruncLE (n : ℤ))

statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a small site and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. For every cochain complex $G$ of $R$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], there exist complexes $E_n$, maps $t_n:E_n\to E_{n+1}$, and termwise epimorphic quasi-isomorphisms $q_n:E_n\to\tau_{\le n}G$ [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], for all $n\in\mathbf N$, such that every $E_n$ is bounded above, every term $E_n^i$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and $t_n q_{n+1}\iota_{n+1}=q_n\iota_n$ as maps into $G$, where $\iota_n:\tau_{\le n}G\to G$ is the good truncation inclusion. Bounded above means that for each $n$ some integer $b_n$ has $E_n^i=0$ for $i>b_n$.

proof.text: Use flat module sheaves as the resolving class. Zero and finite sums are flat [lem-pc-sites-modules-coproduct-flat]. Every module has a flat epimorphic cover by sums of $j_{U!}R_U$ [lem-pc-sites-modules-quotient-j-shriek], using [lem-pc-sites-modules-j-shriek-flat] and [lem-pc-sites-modules-coproduct-flat]. The bounded-above flat replacement theorem [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement] resolves bounded-above complexes in this class. Start with a replacement of $\tau_{\le0}G$.

Inductively resolve the cone of $E_n\to\tau_{\le n+1}G$ by a bounded-above flat complex. Its map to $E_n[1]$ gives an extension complex $E_{n+1}$, degreewise split over $E_n$. Lift and subtract the homotopy of the augmentation square using these splittings, so the square commutes strictly. The long exact cohomology sequences show that the new augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Add the contractible two-term complex from a flat cover of $G^n$ in degrees $n,n+1$. Its map covers degree n and the boundaries in degree n+1. Surjectivity of the augmentation on cohomology supplies the remaining cycles in degree n+1, making the new augmentation epimorphic there as well. In other degrees epimorphisms follow from the preceding augmentation. The contractible addition preserves the quasi-isomorphism; terms remain finite sums of flat objects and bounded above. This is the induction in Derived Categories, lemma-special-direct-system, applied to the flat resolving class.

Compose the strictly commuting squares with the truncation inclusions $\iota_{n+1}$ to obtain $t_n q_{n+1}\iota_{n+1}=q_n\iota_n$. Retain boundedness, flatness, epimorphisms and quasi-isomorphisms from the construction.
